title: Advanced React Patterns
description: Graduate to professional-level React. Master the Context API for global state, React Router for navigation, data fetching patterns, performance optimisation with React.memo, and error boundaries.
learningObjectives: Share global state without prop drilling using Context + useContext
Build multi-page apps with React Router v6
Implement optimistic UI updates and data mutation patterns
Handle runtime errors gracefully with error boundaries

exercises.question: What problem does the Context API primarily solve?
options: Prop drilling — passing props through many intermediate layers
exercises.correctAnswer: Prop drilling — passing props through many intermediate layers
hints: Think about passing a theme through 10 component levels
exercises.explanation: Context provides a channel to 'teleport' data from a provider to any deeply nested consumer without passing props through every intermediate component. It's not a replacement for all state management.

exercises.question: In React Router v6, which component renders the matched child route inside a layout?
hints: It 'outlets' the child into the parent layout
exercises.explanation: <Outlet /> is a placeholder in a parent route's element that renders whichever child route matches. This enables shared layouts (nav, footer) across multiple pages.

sections.content: 🎯 Use the React DevTools Profiler to identify components that re-render frequently. Optimise only components that are measurably slow — not everything.

exercises.question: React.memo prevents a component from re-rendering when:
options: State changes in the component itself
Its parent re-renders but its props haven't changed
The router navigates to a different page
exercises.correctAnswer: Its parent re-renders but its props haven't changed
exercises.explanation: React.memo wraps a component and performs a shallow props comparison. If props are the same as the last render (by reference), React skips re-rendering that component.

exercises.question: What does React.lazy() and Suspense enable?
options: Code splitting — loading component code only when needed
exercises.correctAnswer: Code splitting — loading component code only when needed
hints: 'Lazy' means it loads later, not immediately
exercises.explanation: React.lazy() dynamically imports a component only when it's rendered. Combined with Suspense's fallback, this enables code splitting — the bundle is split and heavy components load on demand, reducing initial load time.

exercises.question: What is the main benefit of the Compound Components pattern?
options: Encapsulates shared state while giving consumers control over structure and rendering
Reduces the number of useState calls
exercises.correctAnswer: Encapsulates shared state while giving consumers control over structure and rendering
hints: Think about how HTML's <select> and <option> work together
exercises.explanation: Compound components share state implicitly through context while exposing composable sub-components. Consumers control the structure — enabling flexible API design without an explosion of configuration props.

capstoneProject.title: Full-Stack React Application
capstoneProject.description: Build a complete multi-page React application with auth, routing, global state, data fetching, error handling, and performance optimization.
requirements: React Router v6 with nested routes and layout
Auth context (login/logout/user state) via Context API
Protected routes that redirect to login
Data fetching with custom useFetch hook + loading/error states
Error Boundary around the main content area
Lazy loaded routes using React.lazy + Suspense
Compound component pattern for a reusable UI element
